articles.body: TITLE: 양자의 그림자: 비트코인 암호 체계, 과연 위협받고 있나? 30년 동안 디지털 세상의 진화를 지켜봐 왔다. 공개 키 암호화의 초기 시절부터 분산원장 혁명에 이르기까지 말이다. 양자 컴퓨팅이 비트코인에 가하는 위협에 대한 질문은 새삼스러운 것은 아니지만, 늘 선정적인 헤드라인과 함께 다시 떠오르곤 한다. 수십 년간 기술 주기를 관찰하며 다듬어진 내 관점은 이렇다. 위협은 분명 실재하지만, 그 시기는 과학적 돌파구와 공학적 난제, 그리고 인간의 적응이 복잡하게 얽혀 결정된다. 당장 종말을 마주한 건 아니지만, 그렇다고 안일하게 있을 수도 없다. 진정한 난제는 양자 컴퓨터가 비트코인의 암호 체계를 깰 수 있는지 가 아니라, 언제 그럴 만한 규모와 안정성을 갖출지, 그리고 비트코인의 분산형 개발이 제때 강력한 대응책을 구현할 수 있는지에 달려 있다. 배경 이러한 위협의 본질을 진정으로 이해하려면, 비트코인이 의존하는 특정 암호화 기본 요소와 이를 공격할 양자 알고리즘을 해부해야 한다. 비트코인의 보안은 크게 두 가지 기둥에 기반을 둔다. 개인 키와 거래를 보호하는 ECDSA(Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm)와 작업 증명(Proof-of-Work) 채굴 및 주소 생성에 사용되는 SHA-256이다. 가장 직접적인 실존적 위협은 Shor's Algorithm 에서 비롯된다. 이것은 이론적인 추측이 아니다. 큰 숫자를 효율적으로 인수분해하고 이산 로그 문제를 해결할 수 있는, 이미 알려진 알고리즘이다. 이 문제들은 ECDSA의 수학적 기초를 이룬다.
articles.author: Record0x

articles.title: The Quantum Shadow: Is Bitcoin's Cryptography Truly at Risk?
articles.excerpt: TITLE: The Quantum Shadow: Is Bitcoin's Cryptography Truly at Risk? For thirty years, I've watched the digital frontier evolve, from the early days of public-key encryption to the distributed ledger r…
articles.body: TITLE: The Quantum Shadow: Is Bitcoin's Cryptography Truly at Risk? For thirty years, I've watched the digital frontier evolve, from the early days of public-key encryption to the distributed ledger revolution. The question of quantum computing's threat to Bitcoin isn't new, but it's one that consistently resurfaces, often accompanied by sensational headlines. My perspective, honed over decades of observing technological cycles, is this: the threat is unequivocally real, but the timeline remains a complex interplay of scientific breakthroughs, engineering hurdles, and human adaptation. We aren't staring down an immediate apocalypse, but neither can we afford complacency.
articles.author: Record0x

articles.title: I got tired of checking ten SEO dashboards, so I built one weekly to-do list
articles.excerpt: How I built the SEO/GEO workspace in KiwiToolkit, and why it doesn't try to automate your SEO for you. I build and run websites. For years, "doing SEO" on them looked the same: Search Console open in…
articles.body: How I built the SEO/GEO workspace in KiwiToolkit, and why it doesn't try to automate your SEO for you. I build and run websites. For years, "doing SEO" on them looked the same: Search Console open in one tab, Google Analytics in another, Bing Webmaster Tools somewhere behind them, a PageSpeed report, a crawler export, a rank tracker, and a spreadsheet of sites I'd asked for a link (and who had actually answered). Every tool reported its own metrics, in its own way, on its own schedule. None of them answered the only question I actually had on a Monday morning: How am I doing, and what should I fix this week? So most weeks, nothing got checked. Not because I didn't care, but because getting a clear picture took an hour of tab-switching before I could do anything useful.

articles.title: Live Hair Colour Try-On, Entirely on the Phone: MediaPipe in a WebView Inside Flutter
articles.excerpt: In the Miraviso Colore app you point the front camera at your face, tap a copper brown, and your hair turns copper brown while you move your head. No frame leaves the phone. Put like that it sounds li…
articles.body: In the Miraviso Colore app you point the front camera at your face, tap a copper brown, and your hair turns copper brown while you move your head. No frame leaves the phone. Put like that it sounds like a filter app feature. Doing it properly, on an ordinary Android phone and with a privacy promise you can check by watching the network, took more rounds than I had planned for. This is the engine as it stands today, with the numbers I measured. Why there is a browser inside a Flutter app The first thing that surprises people who open the code: the try-on does not use tflite_flutter , there is no Kotlin plugin and no Flutter shader. The screen is a WebViewWidget , and inside it runs a page with MediaPipe Tasks Vision in WebAssembly and a WebGL2 fragment shader.
articles.author: Gabriele Pieretti

articles.title: Software May Help Decide Your Next Promotion
articles.excerpt: More companies are buying tools that use AI to help manage people. Some summarise your work into draft performance reviews. Some suggest who is ready for promotion based on project data. Some score ac…
articles.body: More companies are buying tools that use AI to help manage people. Some summarise your work into draft performance reviews. Some suggest who is ready for promotion based on project data. Some score activity in the tools you use every day. They are sold as a way to make decisions fairer and faster, and some of them may well help. The law is starting to take this seriously. The European Union's AI Act treats AI systems used to make decisions about promotion and termination, to allocate work based on people's behaviour or traits, or to monitor and evaluate workers' performance, as high risk. That brings obligations for the companies that build and use them, including human oversight.
articles.author: Asael Shinder

articles.title: Texture Atlases for a Browser Game Map
articles.excerpt: Originally published on the DENSHIN blog. The first thing we want you to see when you open Denshin is a readable city. The street markings help with that. A car turning onto an avenue helps the city f…
articles.body: Originally published on the DENSHIN blog . The first thing we want you to see when you open Denshin is a readable city. The street markings help with that. A car turning onto an avenue helps the city feel alive, but the map can already tell you where you are before the car arrives. Those two jobs look similar in the art folder. They shouldn't have the same place in the loading queue. We pack the road markings and the vehicles into separate texture atlases . Here's what an atlas changes, how we keep the images in the right place, and why we don't put all the map art on the same sheet. One image, many named rectangles A texture atlas is an image containing many smaller pictures. A companion file gives each picture a name and describes its rectangle on the sheet.

articles.title: How to stop a runaway AI agent loop before it runs up your OpenAI or Anthropic bill
articles.excerpt: TL;DR: A runaway agent loop shows up in your API traffic before it shows up on your bill. It looks like the same call repeated fast, or a context that keeps doubling. Tag every LLM call with the produ…
articles.body: TL;DR: A runaway agent loop shows up in your API traffic before it shows up on your bill. It looks like the same call repeated fast, or a context that keeps doubling. Tag every LLM call with the product feature it belongs to. Watch the last few calls per feature. When they look like a loop, throttle that one feature first and block it if the loop continues. This post has a small TypeScript circuit breaker you can copy, the limits of doing it yourself, and how the existing tools (LiteLLM, Helicone, Portkey, Langfuse and AtlasBurn) handle it. Disclosure: I build AtlasBurn , one of the tools compared below. The DIY code works without it. Why provider spend limits don't save you OpenAI and Anthropic let you set a monthly budget or alert on the whole account.
articles.author: Akhil Anand

articles.excerpt: The second film in Clint Eastwood's "The Man with No Name Trilogy," For a Few Dollars More, is free on youtube, making this perfect time to watch
articles.body: In 1964, Italian director Sergio Leone redefined the Western movie genre with A Fistful of Dollars . Eschewing the relatively simplistic morality tales of earlier films, Leone’s protagonist wasn’t a noble hero, but an opportunistic gunslinger who pits two rival Old West gangs against each other to score a big payday. Despite the moral complexity of it all — or, more likely, because of it — A Fistful of Dollars was an international success that proved three things: audiences were ready for a new kind of Western, America no longer had a monopoly on the genre, and Clint Eastwood was a bankable movie star.

articles.body: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force from California tonight (Nov. 11), the second such flight for the company in a six-day span. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base tonight at 11:36 p.m. EST (8:36 p.m. local California time; 0136 GMT on Nov. 12), kicking off a mission called USSF-627. Vandenberg hosted a similar liftoff less than a week ago: On Nov. 6, a Falcon 9 sent the USSF-432 mission skyward from the site, which lies on California's gorgeous but often foggy central coast. A Falcon 9 first stage rests on a SpaceX drone ship shortly after launching the USSF-627 mission on Nov. 11, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) We don't know much about USSF-627 or USSF-432; both are classified.

articles.title: Constantine Director 'Hopeful' for Sequel After DC Studios Shakeup
articles.excerpt: The director of Constantine, Francis Lawrence, opened up about the movie's long-awaited sequel now that DC Studios has had a changing of the guard.
articles.body: The director of Constantine, Francis Lawrence, opened up about the movie's long-awaited sequel now that DC Studios has had a changing of the guard. James Gunn and Peter Safran are out at DC Studios in a sudden and unexpected move that has sparked no end of worry and speculation among fans. Gunn, for his part, cited a distaste for the “corporate” side of the job, but confirmed that projects already in motion, like Man of Tomorrow , are still a-go. Fans aren’t the only ones scratching their heads about what might happen next. Francis Lawrence, the director of oodles of Hollywood blockbusters, is also in this boat — though he’s rather optimistic about the situation, as it means he might finally get the chance to make another Constantine film.

articles.title: NASA kick-starts a fresh push to bring Mars samples home
articles.excerpt: NASA is kickstarting a new initiative for Mars Sample Return (MSR), called the Perseverance Sample Retrieval Architecture.
articles.body: A long-term goal at NASA has been the ability to robotically haul back to Earth specimens from the Red Planet. NASA is kickstarting a new initiative for its troubled Mars Sample Return (MSR) program, called the Perseverance Sample Retrieval Architecture, or PSRA in space shorthand. The plan is to establish a fresh NASA strategy for gathering Mars samples collected by the Perseverance rover and launching them back to Earth. The PSRA initiative was noted on Nov. 9 by Tiffany Morgan, director of the NASA Mars Exploration Program (MEP), during the virtual meeting of the Mars Exploration Program Analysis Group (MEPAG).

articles.title: We can't see Fast Radio Bursts but we can now hear them thanks to a Finnish Cathedral
articles.excerpt: Fast radio bursts are invisible, but a composer has turned thousands of them into sound at a Finnish cathedral, where a choir will sing along on Nov. 21.
articles.body: Fast radio bursts, flashes of energy from faraway galaxies, are invisible to our eyes. However, we can now hear their melody, thanks to a composer who has turned them into sound. Fast radio bursts, or FRBs , are among the most extreme events in the universe, releasing as much energy in a millisecond as the sun puts out in three days and briefly outshining entire galaxies. Since the first FRB was discovered in 2007, astronomers have detected thousands of them; however, exactly how these cosmic flares are launched remains poorly understood. Recent evidence points to at least one burst coming from the environment around a rotating neutron star. Despite their power, FRBs last only a few thousandths of a second before vanishing into space.
